subject: Non-prod zone exclusion & PrivateLink clearance for Mediq Health pilot
messages:
From: ops@mediqhealth.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: legal@mediqhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-12 09:18 PDT
Subject: Request: exclude certain US zones from pilot + PrivateLink peering request

Hi David,

Quick one as we prep the Mediq Health pilot — security has flagged a requirement to explicitly exclude two AWS availability zones in us-west-2 (us-west-2b and us-west-2c) from our non-production footprint for regulatory validation. Can Redwood provide a short confirmation that non-prod workloads for our pilot can be restricted to us-west-2a (or alternate approved subnets) so that our audit trail is clear?

Separately, our infra team wants to use PrivateLink (privatelink) peering for the pilot. They asked for:
- a short design doc showing endpoint types and expected egress paths
- operator contact for setup and testing
- any CAIQ/SIG artifacts that reference PrivateLink or VPC-isolation controls

I attached a CSV with the exact zone list and a short timeline for the pilot. We need a response by 2026-10-20 to keep the onboarding slot.

Thanks —
Alex Carver
Head of Ops, Mediq Health
ops@mediqhealth.com


From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: ops@mediqhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-13 10:04 PDT
Subject: Re: Request: exclude certain US zones from pilot + PrivateLink peering request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the CSV. Short answers up front:

1) Non-prod zone exclusion: yes, we can restrict your non-prod tenant to a single AZ within the requested region for the pilot. We will implement subnet-level placement constraints and record the allocation in the onboarding runbook.

2) PrivateLink: we support PrivateLink endpoints into our VPCs for Private deployments. For hosted/Dedicated pilots we provide a managed endpoint configuration; for Private (VPC) we provide an operator checklist to establish the peer.

I'm looping in Marissa from Security for the CAIQ/SIG extraction and Hannah from Solutions for the peer design and operator contact. Marissa — can you confirm which CAIQ/CAIQ-derived answers reference PrivateLink and VPC isolation and attach the latest snapshot? Hannah — we should prepare a concise design (2 pages) describing the endpoint type, DNS flow, expected egress, and a short test plan. I can commit to turnaround by EOD 2026-10-19.

Next steps:
- Marissa: CAIQ snapshot + SOC2 mapping for PrivateLink controls
- Hannah: PrivateLink design PDF + operator on-call name/phone
- David: confirm non-prod subnet annotation and sign-off language for Mediq's audit pack

Dave
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi all — attaching the CAIQ-snapshot-answers-20261019.xlsx with highlighted rows that map to network isolation and private connectivity controls (NIST/CCM crosswalks included). Summary notes below: 

- CAIQ / SIG: Questions referencing VPC endpoints, private connectivity, and egress controls are annotated in sheet "Network + Connectivity." The answers indicate our standard architecture for Dedicated and Private deployments (we reference PrivateLink for managed ingress and VPC peering for on-prem).
- SOC 2 evidence: for the pilot we can provide the SOC 2 artifact pointers (control IDs) that demonstrate network segregation and change management; we won't share raw logs but can provide the evidence indexes and redacted control outputs for your compliance team.
- Zone exclusion: to confirm David's note — we will annotate your tenant as "non-prod: us-west-2a only" in the onboarding runbook and in the provisioning tags. This will be captured in INF-4281 (ticket link below).

Attachments:
- CAIQ-snapshot-answers-20261019.xlsx (contains answer extract + crosswalk)
- quick-annotated-index.txt (list of SOC 2 artifacts and where to find them in our evidence vault)

Note on limitations and recommended language for your auditors: we can confirm the provisioned placement for non-prod for the duration of the pilot (dates inclusive); if you require contract-level geographic guarantees we should escalate to Legal to add a limited SLA clause.

Jonas from Ops — FYI I marked the PrivateLink design questions in the sheet that require an operator for testing (DNS verification, 3-way handshake, and traffic flow sample captures).

—Marissa
